meta_desc: Step-by-step NCERT Class 12 Determinants Miscellaneous Exercise solutions on properties, cofactors, adjoint, inverse and systems, plus a free quiz.

quiz.title: Class 12 Determinants Miscellaneous Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight mixed questions on determinant properties, cofactors, adjoint, inverse and solving systems. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If A is a 3×3 matrix with |A| = 5, what is |3A|?
questions.explanation: For an n×n matrix, |kA| = k<sup>n</sup>|A|. Here n = 3, so |3A| = 3<sup>3</sup> × 5 = 27 × 5 = 135.

questions.q: For a square matrix A of order 3, |adj A| equals:
questions.explanation: For order n, |adj A| = |A|<sup>n-1</sup>. With n = 3 this gives |A|<sup>2</sup>.

questions.q: If A is invertible of order 3 and |A| = 2, then |A<sup>-1</sup>| is:
The value of the determinant of a matrix equals the value of its transpose because:
options: Rows and columns can be swapped without changing the value
questions.explanation: A key property: |A| = |A<sup>T</sup>|. Interchanging rows into columns leaves the determinant unchanged.

questions.q: If two rows of a determinant are identical, its value is:
questions.explanation: A determinant with two identical (or proportional) rows is 0. This property is used often to prove identities in the miscellaneous exercise.

questions.q: The cofactor C<sub>ij</sub> of an element a<sub>ij</sub> is defined as:
questions.explanation: The cofactor is the signed minor: C<sub>ij</sub> = (-1)<sup>i+j</sup> M<sub>ij</sub>, where M<sub>ij</sub> is the minor obtained by deleting row i and column j.

questions.q: For a nonsingular matrix A, A<sup>-1</sup> is given by:
questions.explanation: The inverse formula is A<sup>-1</sup> = (1/|A|) adj A, valid only when |A| ≠ 0.

questions.q: A system AX = B of linear equations has a unique solution when:
questions.explanation: If |A| ≠ 0, A is invertible and X = A<sup>-1</sup>B gives a unique solution — the consistency test used throughout this exercise.

faq.q: What does the Determinants Miscellaneous Exercise cover?
faq.a: It mixes every idea from the chapter: applying determinant properties to evaluate or simplify, finding minors and cofactors, computing the adjoint and inverse, proving algebraic identities, and solving systems of linear equations using |A| and A<sup>-1</sup>.

faq.q: Which determinant properties are most useful here?
faq.a: The ones that let you create zeros: |A| = |A<sup>T</sup>|, a row/column of zeros gives 0, two identical or proportional rows give 0, and adding a multiple of one row to another leaves the value unchanged. Row and column operations are the fastest route through most miscellaneous problems.

faq.q: How do I find the inverse of a 3×3 matrix in this exercise?
faq.a: First compute |A|; if it is nonzero, find the cofactor of every element, form the cofactor matrix, transpose it to get adj A, then use A<sup>-1</sup> = (1/|A|) adj A. Verify by checking A A<sup>-1</sup> = I.

faq.q: How are systems of equations solved using determinants?
faq.a: Write the system as AX = B. If |A| ≠ 0 the solution is unique and X = A<sup>-1</sup>B. If |A| = 0 the system is either inconsistent or has infinitely many solutions, which you test using the matrix method.
